Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:10:1.hebrew: ה"ק ולהטעינה - ולעולם דאורייתא, ורישא תנא מטפל בה בין בפריקה בין בטעינה: פריקה משום צער בעלי חיים, וטעינה משום איבה. ולהטעינה יין אסור, דלאו צערא איכא ולאו איבה איכא, אין זקוק לה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:10:1.english: This is what [the tanna] is saying: And to load it - In fact, [preventing the suffering of animals is] by Torah law, and the first clause taught [that] he attends to it, whether in unloading or in loading: unloading [is] because of the suffering of living creatures, and loading [is] because of enmity. And to load it with forbidden wine — where there is neither suffering nor enmity — he does not attend to it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:11:1.hebrew: התם בטעינה - לקמיה פריך, הא בפריקה כתיב:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:11:1.english: There, [it refers to] loading - Further on, [the Gemara] asks: Isn't [the verse] written regarding unloading?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:12:1.english: Because of the suffering of the Jew - For he needs to wait there.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:13:1.hebrew: בחמר עובד כוכבים - ואין בעל המשא שם, ועל העובד כוכבים לטעון:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:13:1.english: With a gentile donkey driver - And the owner of the burden is not there, and it is upon the gentile to load [it].

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:13:2.hebrew: מאי פסקת - וכי פסקת הדבר כן, דכל בהמת עובד כוכבים הוי חמר עובד כוכבים, וכל בהמת ישראל הוי חמר ישראל:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:13:2.english: What [basis do] you decide [this on] - Do you really decide the matter thus: that every animal of an idolater has an idolater [as its] donkey driver, and every animal of a Jew has a Jewish donkey driver?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:17:1.hebrew: שונא שאמרו - קס"ד שונא שאמרו אשונא דקרא קאי, דמשתעי בפריקה, כי תראה חמור שונאך רובץ וגומר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:17:1.english: The enemy of whom they spoke - [The Gemara] initially assumed [that] "the enemy of whom they spoke" refers to the enemy [mentioned] in the verse, which speaks of unloading: "If you see the donkey of your enemy crouching, etc."

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:18:1.hebrew: אשונא דמתניתין קאי - אהך מתניתא דלעיל, דשונא לטעון הוא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:18:1.english: It refers to the enemy of the baraita - To that baraita [cited] above, where [the case of] an enemy is to load.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:1.english: From the statements of both of them - Since both of them say unloading is preferable.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:2.hebrew: ואפילו ר"ש לא קאמר - דאצטריך למכתב פריקה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:2.english: And even Rabbi Shimon did not say - that it was necessary to write unloading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:3.english: Only because the verses are not clearly defined - [As referring] to loading.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:4.hebrew: לאו משום צער בעלי חיים - והכי יליף: מה טעינה דליכא צער בעלי חיים, חייב; פריקה דאיכא צער בעלי חיים, לא כ"ש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:1:4.english: [Is it] not due to [the] suffering of animals - And thus it derives [it]: If [regarding] loading, where there is no suffering of animals, [one is] obligated; [then regarding] unloading, where there is suffering of animals, [is it] not all the more so?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:3:1.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן - וכי אין המקרא מדבר אף בהולך לסחורה, דאדהכי בטיל משוקיה:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:3:1.english: Are we not dealing - Does the verse not also speak of one going for merchandise, so that in the meantime he is prevented from [reaching] his market?

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:1.hebrew: תדע - דלרבנן דפליגי עליה דר"ש, ולר"ש, צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:1.english: Know - That according to the Rabbis who disagree with Rabbi Shimon, and according to Rabbi Shimon, [preventing] suffering to animals is by Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:2.hebrew: מכלל דת"ק - דרבי יוסי הגלילי, רבנן ור"ש:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:2.english: By inference that the first tanna - of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili [refers to] the Rabbis and Rabbi Shimon:

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:3.hebrew: זקוק לו - ואמאי זקוק לו? אי משום מצות עזב תעזב, הא כתיב משאו — הראוי לו; אלא משום צער בעלי חיים:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:4:3.english: He must attend to it - And why must he attend to it? If [it is] because of the mitzvah of "you shall surely help unload" [Exodus 23:5], behold, it is written "its burden" — [meaning that which is] fitting for it; rather, [it is] because of [preventing] suffering to animals.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:5:1.hebrew: לא דרשינן משאו - למשא הראוי לו, דמשאו כל משא שעליו משמע:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:5:1.english: We do not interpret “its burden” - [to refer] to a burden that is suitable for it, for “its burden” implies any burden that is upon it.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:6:1.hebrew: ותדע - דהכי הוא כדדחינא לך, דצער בעלי חיים לאו דאורייתא:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:6:1.english: And know - that it is so as I deflected [the proof] for you, that [preventing] suffering to animals is not by Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:7:1.hebrew: עביד גביה - משום צער בעלי חיים, ועל כורחו יטול שכר:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:7:1.english: Perform [the unloading] for him - Because of [preventing] suffering to animals, and against his [the owner's] will he takes a wage.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:9:1.english: Let us say [it] supports him - [Namely,] Rava, who said above [that preventing] the suffering of living creatures is by Torah law.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:9:2.english: He tends to it - To unload its burden.

Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:9:3.hebrew: אי אמרת לאו דאורייתא - וטעמא משום איבה הוא, מש"ה אין זקוק לה, שיכול להשמט ולומר דבר איסור הוא לנו:
Rashi on Bava Metzia 32b:9:3.english: If you say [it is] not by Torah law - and the reason [one tends to a gentile's animal] is because of enmity, therefore he is not obligated [to tend] to it [when it is carrying libation wine], for he can excuse himself and say, "It is a forbidden item for us."

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:10:1.hebrew: ולהטעינה יין אסור אין זקוק לה - אבל שאר דברים זקוק, ואפילו לטעון, משום איבה:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:10:1.english: And to load it with forbidden wine he does not attend to it - But [with] other things he is obligated [to attend to it], and even to load [it], because of enmity.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:11:1.hebrew: אמאי וחדלת - וא"ת ולישני: בחנם, אבל בשכר חייב, ולעולם צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא? וי"ל דוחדלת משמע לגמרי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:11:1.english: Why "you shall forgo"? - And if you should ask: Why not answer [that "you shall forgo" means] for free, whereas for a fee he is obligated, and in fact [preventing] suffering to animals is by Torah law? And one can answer that "you shall forgo" implies [forgoing] completely [even for a fee].

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:12:1.hebrew: ואי בטעינה אמאי עזוב - וליכא למימר דבטיל משוקיה, דאם כן רישא נמי:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:12:1.english: And if [it is referring to] loading, why [does it say] “you shall release it” - And one cannot say [that the reason is] because he is delayed from his market, for if so, [that would apply to] the first clause as well.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:16:1.hebrew: לכוף יצרו - וא"ת, כיון דבערבי פסחים (שם) מוקי לה בישראל שמותר לשנאותו, כגון שראה בו דבר ערוה, מה שייך בו לכוף יצרו? וי"ל דלא מיירי בשונא דקרא:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:16:1.english: To subjugate his inclination - And if you ask: since in [the chapter] Arvei Pesachim (ibid.) [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to a Jew whom it is permitted to hate, such as where one saw an unseemly matter in him, how does "subjugating his inclination" apply to him? And one can answer that [the baraita] is not speaking of the enemy [mentioned] in the verse:

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:17:1.hebrew: מה לי שונא עובד כוכבים - ה"מ לשנויי: ישראל בחנם, ולעובד כוכבים בשכר:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:17:1.english: What is it to me [if it is] a gentile enemy? - [The Gemara] could have answered: [Assisting] a Jew [is] for free, whereas for a gentile [it is] for payment.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:1:1.hebrew: מדברי שניהם נלמד צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא - וא"ת: א"כ, אמאי עוקרים על המלכים, ולא מדרכי האמורי (ע"ז דף יא.)? וי"ל: משום דכבוד מלך ונשיא עדיף, כמו בל תשחית דנדחה מפני כבודם, דאונקלוס שרף על ר"ג ע' מנה צורי פ"ק דע"ז (שם). ועוד: דכיון דכתיב "את סוסיהם תעקר", קל לדחות מפני המלך:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:1:1.english: From the statements of both of them it is learned that [the prohibition against] causing suffering to animals is by Torah law - And if you say: If so, why do we hamstring [animals] for kings, and [it is] not [prohibited as part] of the ways of the Amorites (Avodah Zarah 11a)? And one can answer: Because the honor of a king or a Nasi takes precedence, just like [the prohibition of] "do not destroy" (bal tashchit), which is overridden for their honor — as Onkelos burned seventy Tyrian manehs for Rabban Gamliel, [as stated in] the first chapter of Avodah Zarah (ibid.). And furthermore: Since it is written, "You shall hamstring their horses," it is easily overridden for the king.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:3:1.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן דאדהכי והכי בטיל משוקיה - וא"ת, מ"מ נדרוש ק"ו מטעינה דלית בה חסרון כיס? וי"ל: כיון דטעינה שיש בה חסרון כיס לא הוי בשכר, דמ"ש מפריקה — א"כ אף טעינה דלית בה חסרון כיס נמי הוי בחנם, ופריקה נכתבה לדרוש שום דרשה אחרת:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:3:1.english: "Are we not dealing [with a case] where in the meanwhile he is prevented from [going to] his marketplace" - And if you will say: Nevertheless, let us derive an a fortiori inference from [a case of] loading where there is no monetary loss! One can answer: Since loading where there is monetary loss is not [done] for a fee — for how is it different from unloading? — if so, even loading where there is no monetary loss is also [done] for free, and [the verse of] unloading was written to expound some other exposition.

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:4:1.hebrew: מכלל דת"ק סבר דזקוק לו - המקשה סבור דת"ק נמי ידרוש "משאו" שהוא יכול לעמוד בו, ושאינו יכול לעמוד בו — נהי דאין חייב לסייע בחנם משום דלית ביה מצות פריקה, מ"מ בשכר חייב לסייעו משום צער בעלי חיים. וא"ת: ולרבי יוסי הגלילי, דסבר צער בעלי חיים לאו דאורייתא, ואית ליה לקמן (בבא מציעא דף לג.) דטעינה בשכר — מ"ש טעינה מפריקה? וי"ל: דדריש ק"ו מחסרון כיס, דלכתוב טעינה גרידא, דיש טעינה שאין בו חסרון כיס וכ"ש פריקה; אלא כתב פריקה לאגמורי דטעינה בשכר. וכיון דטעינה שאין בה חסרון כיס הויא בשכר, היכא דאית בה חסרון כיס נמי — דהיינו היכא דבטיל משוקיה — הוי בשכר, דילפי' מטעינה דלית בה חסרון כיס. והשתא לא בא להוכיח רק דצער בעלי חיים דאורייתא, ולא לקיים שמכח ק"ו יש להוכיח דצער בעלי חיים דאורייתא — דאפשר שק"ו הוי מחסרון כיס, כדפרישית לר' יוסי. וא"ת: ודלמא זקוק לו מדרבנן? וי"ל: דכל הסוגיא מוכחת דאי צער בעלי חיים לאו דאורייתא אינו חייב לסייעו אפי' בשכר, כדאמרינן בסמוך: "וכי ליתיה למריה בהדיה ליעבד גביה בשכר", ולעולם צער בעלי חיים דאורייתא; אבל אי הוי דרבנן, פטור היה אפילו בשכר. וכן בתר הכי דקאמר: "ואי אמרת לאו דאורייתא אמאי מטפל ביה?" — ולישני מדרבנן:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:4:1.english: By inference that the first tanna holds that he must attend to it - The questioner assumes that the first tanna also expounds "its burden" [as] a burden that it can bear; and [as for] a burden that it cannot bear — granted that one is not obligated to assist for free, because there is no mitzva of unloading in it, nevertheless for wages one is obligated to assist him because of [preventing] suffering to animals. And if you ask: According to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who holds that [preventing] suffering to animals is not by Torah law, and who holds later (Bava Metzia 33a) that loading is for wages, what is the difference between loading and unloading? And one can answer: He expounds an a fortiori inference from monetary loss — for let [the Torah] write loading alone, as there is [a case of] loading in which there is no monetary loss, and all the more so unloading! Rather, it wrote unloading to teach that loading is for wages. And since loading in which there is no monetary loss is for wages, where there is monetary loss as well — namely, where he is prevented from [reaching] his marketplace — it is also for wages, for we learn [it] from loading in which there is no monetary loss. And now [the Gemara] comes only to prove that [preventing] suffering to animals is by Torah law, and not to uphold [the claim] that by force of the a fortiori inference one can prove that [preventing] suffering to animals is by Torah law — for it is possible that the a fortiori inference is from monetary loss, as I explained according to Rabbi Yosei. And if you ask: Perhaps he must attend to it by rabbinic law? And one can answer: The entire sugya proves that if [preventing] suffering to animals is not by Torah law, one is not obligated to assist him even for wages, as [the Gemara] says shortly thereafter: "And when its owner is not with him, let him work with him for wages," and indeed [preventing] suffering to animals is by Torah law; however, if it were rabbinic, he would be exempt even for wages. And similarly afterward, when it says: "And if you say it is not by Torah law, why does he attend to it?" — let it answer [that it is] by rabbinic law!

Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:9:1.hebrew: ואי לאו דאורייתא אמאי מטפל בה - וא"ת, והלא בספרי דורש "שונאך" — אפילו שונא עובד כוכבים? וי"ל דאסמכתא בעלמא היא, דבערבי פסחים (פסחים דף קיג: ושם) מוקי בשונא ישראל:
Tosafot on Bava Metzia 32b:9:1.english: And if [it is] not by Torah law, why does he tend to it - And if you ask: Does it not expound in the Sifrei [that the verse] "your enemy" [refers] even [to] an idolatrous enemy? One can answer that it is merely an asmakhta [a scriptural allusion], for in [chapter] Arvei Pesachim (Pesachim 113b and there) it establishes [the verse] as referring to a Jewish enemy.
